content: Patients with a history of severe allergic reactions, such as anaphylaxis, to any known components of the product should not use it. Patients must inform their physician if they experience persistent diarrhea, defined as three or more loose bowel movements within a 24-hour period for two consecutive days, after receiving the product. Patients should also be instructed not to take any oral antibiotic therapy for up to eight weeks following product administration unless specifically directed by their physician. Studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk, making the product generally acceptable for use during pregnancy. This microbiota-based live biotherapeutic is administered rectally to deliver a diverse consortium of microbes to the gut, aiming to reduce recurrent Clostridioides difficile infections following antibiotic treatment. The exact mechanism of action has not been established. Before use, the product must be completely thawed by placing the carton in a refrigerator at 2–8°C (36–46°F) for approximately 24 hours. It should not be refrozen after thawing. The thawed carton can be stored in the refrigerator at 2–8°C and used within five days, including the thawing time. Thawing should not be done using heat sources such as microwaves or hot water. Condensation after thawing is normal. To prepare for administration, remove the thawed microbiota bag from the outer and inner cartons, but do not remove it from the sealed outer bag. Locate the administration set (provided), a water-soluble lubricant (not included), and a disposable underpad (not included). Refer to the prescribing information for detailed instructions on setting up the bag for administration. The product is for rectal administration only. Before administration, the patient should empty their bladder and bowel, if possible. Position the patient on their left side or in a knee-chest position. Apply a water-soluble lubricant to the tip of the administration tube, and gently insert the tube approximately 12 cm (5 inches) into the rectum, angling slightly toward the umbilicus. Hold the tube in place with one hand throughout the procedure to maintain its position in the rectum. With the other hand, open the pinch clamp on the administration tube and gradually raise the bag to allow delivery via gravity flow. Do not squeeze the bag, as this may cause patient discomfort, and do not hang the bag from an IV stand. Once the entire dose has been delivered, close the pinch clamp and slowly withdraw the tube, taking care to prevent any residual suspension in the tube from leaking out (some suspension will remain in the tube after administration). After the dose is delivered, keep the patient in the same position for up to 15 minutes to minimize cramping. Dispose of all administration components as medical waste. The product contains live microorganisms, so storage requirements must be followed carefully. Adding plans allows for the comparison of formulary status with other drugs in the same class.
